title: +R, -R and Hyperconjugation Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Pump air in at one valve and the whole tyre fills evenly. Four friends lift a bench more easily than one. Aarav knows the tertiary carbocation is the most stable, but its C-H bonds are not even touching the plus carbon, so how can they help? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) we see two ways electrons spread out.

On the molecule bench, curved arrows push the lone pair of aniline into the ring, moving a minus charge to ortho, para and the other ortho carbon, so ortho and para get richer (+R), while nitrobenzene makes them poorer (-R). In the ethyl cation, a C-H pair leans into the empty p orbital and shares the plus charge: hyperconjugation. Alpha hydrogens are counted (0, 3, 6, 9) to explain carbocation stability, then the four types of organic reactions. A worked example counts alpha hydrogens in the 2-butyl cation, then an exam trap, an original exam pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 85 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
